question: What is the main purpose of development committees in Nigerian primary health care?

options.A: To replace trained doctors in rural clinics
options.B: To encourage community participation and local ownership
options.C: To collect taxes for hospital construction
options.D: To manage federal medical centers directly

explanation: These committees exist to involve local people so they can take charge of their own health needs and partner effectively with health workers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why are local leaders and traditional rulers included in primary health care committees?

options.A: They possess formal medical degrees to diagnose patients
options.B: They are responsible for paying health worker salaries
options.C: They help mobilize the community and build trust in health programs
options.D: They supply all the drugs needed for the clinic

explanation: Traditional and community leaders wield great influence, making it easier to convince villagers to accept immunizations and other health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which committee operates closest to individual households in a rural Nigerian setting?
explanation: The Village Development Committee is the lowest tier, sitting directly within the community to handle immediate local health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h2)

question: A Ward Development Committee is primarily responsible for what task?

options.B: Conducting major surgeries in rural health posts
options.C: Importing foreign medical equipment for teaching hospitals
options.D: Coordinating health activities across multiple villages within a ward

explanation: The ward level brings several villages together to pool resources, oversee local primary health clinics, and coordinate broader community health efforts. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h2)

question: Who is typically a member of a Health Facility Development Committee?

options.C: Federal ministers of finance and education
options.D: State governors and local government chairmen

explanation: The HFDC brings together the people working inside the clinic and the community members using the services to ensure smooth daily operations. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h3)

question: A primary health clinic has a leaking roof and constant drug shortages. Which local committee is best positioned to address this at the facility level?
explanation: The HFDC operates directly at the clinic level, making them the direct body to monitor facility maintenance and local drug supplies. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h3)

question: Who usually chairs the Local Government Area PHC Development Committee?

options.A: The LGA Chairman or health supervisor
options.B: The Director of World Health Organization

explanation: Political leadership at the local government level, specifically the chairman or health supervisor, leads this committee to ensure administrative and financial backing. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main function of the LGA PHC Development Committee?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines for the entire country
options.B: Treating emergency trauma cases at teaching hospitals
options.C: Designing the national university medical curriculum
options.D: Allocating resources and coordinating health services across the entire local government

explanation: The LGA committee oversees all primary health care activities within its local government area, ensuring fair distribution of resources and personnel. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is a major role of state-level primary health care bodies in Nigeria?

options.B: Collecting local market taxes for traditional rulers
options.C: Appointing village chiefs in rural communities
options.D: Supervising LGA activities and procuring bulk medical supplies

explanation: State bodies provide mid-level oversight, supporting local governments with supplies, training, and technical guidance. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why are national implementation committees necessary for primary health care?

options.A: To prescribe individual drugs to rural patients
options.B: To set standard policies, coordinate donor support, and evaluate nationwide health goals
options.C: To replace local government chairmen during elections
options.D: To manage the daily cleaning of every village health post

explanation: National committees ensure uniformity in health service delivery, manage national funds, and guide the overall direction of the country's health sector. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by PHC development committees in Nigeria?

options.B: Lack of transport for community outreach
options.C: Excessive, surplus funding with no way to spend it

explanation: Committees almost always suffer from underfunding and resource scarcity rather than having too much money. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why does a lack of financial transparency harm grassroots health committees?

options.A: It destroys community trust and discourages local donations and participation
options.B: It causes international pharmaceutical companies to raise drug prices
options.C: It forces health workers to close all clinics permanently
options.D: It automatically stops the federal government from paying nurse salaries

explanation: When villagers suspect mismanagement of local health funds, they lose faith in the committee and refuse to support health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h6)
